label: Late original-phase input of d/r/m/a/b/s/l in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the original phase (95% of mass) and on <DEL> (5%), never in the copy phase. It is silent for t<=4 and is concentrated at t=6..8 of long sequences (L=8,9 hold 90% of mass), within the last ~3 tokens before <DEL>; the rate climbs with orig_idx (20% at orig_idx 8). Input-token identity strongly modulates it: d (5x lift), r, m, a, b, s, l are preferred, i/k/w are weaker, and most other tokens rarely trigger it. Activation is larger on the first occurrence of a token and when the sequence starts with e/t/c/3/v. The strongest activations are d or r at the final original step (t=8 for L=9), and the following <DEL> often fires weakly too. Even under these conditions it fires only about a third of the time, so it seems to depend on more of the hidden-state context than this predicate captures. Dev F1 is about 0.45, with mass recall 0.75.
